newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa Transnet plans return to profit in 96/97.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa Transnet plans return to profit in 96/97.

text.p: Transnet, the South African transportation parastatal, said on Wednesday it planned to return to profit in the 1996/97 financial year with results for the first five months looking promising.
Announcing a slide into loss in the year to end-March 1996, Saki Macozoma, Transnet's newly appointed managing director said: "We certainly plan to return to profitability."
Transnet executive director Gloria Serobe added: "The first five months are showing positive results."
Transnet on Wednesday reported a loss of 253 million rand for the year, compared to a 118 million rand profit a year ago, with the PX and Spoornet divisions the poorest performers.
Transnet subsidiaries include South African Airways (SAA), Autonet (road transport), Petronet (oil pipeline), Spoornet (railways), PX (container and parcel delivery) and Portnet (ports).

PX, which saw its net loss for the year deepen to 433 million rand from 297 million rand before was in line for a comprehensive restructuring and streamlining, a document released by Transnet on Wednesday and recently submitted to parliament shows.

If the process was successful, Transnet said it expected current loss projections of 358 million rand for PX in 1996/97 to be reduced to less than 295 million rand, with the company breaking even in the 1997/98 year.

Spoornet, which saw net profit plunge to 98 million rand from 734 million a year ago, expected an improvement in earnings helped by a substantial increase in maize transport due to a bumper crop this season, chief executive Braam le Roux said.
"Our budgeted turnover from maize this year is 200 million rand compared to the 17 million we made last year," le Roux told Reuters.

Other divisions reported modest improvements in earnings with Petronet lifting profits to 180 million rand from 144 million rand, Autonet 23 million rand from 20 million rand, SAA a leap to 324 million rand from 217 million rand and Portnet 1.4 billion rand from 1.1 billion rand.
Transnet is one of the South African state assets earmarked for privatisation and was recently chosen as the second sector to be assessed for privatisation after telecommunications.
